name: Short QT Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Gollob Criteria for Short QT Syndrome

criteria.description: Pathogenic mutation in known SQTS-associated genes (e.g., KCNH2, KCNQ1, KCNJ2)
History of ventricular arrhythmias or sudden cardiac arrest
Family history of SQTS or sudden cardiac death at young age

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: QTc interval ≤ 330 ms plus either a pathogenic mutation or clinical history of ventricular arrhythmia/sudden cardiac arrest
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by family history and genetic testing; clinical context is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormally short QT interval on ECG

pathognomonic.notes: Includes ventricular fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia

common.notes: Transient loss of consciousness due to arrhythmia

occasional.notes: May result from arrhythmia or reduced cardiac output
Often related to transient cerebral hypoperfusion

rare.notes: Rare but reported in neonatal SQTS cases
Secondary to cerebral hypoxia during arrhythmia

genetic: Pathogenic variants in KCNH2, KCNQ1, KCNJ2, or other ion channel genes
other: Family history of sudden cardiac death
Electrophysiological study showing short refractory periods

distinguishingFeatures: Prolonged QT interval instead of shortened
Different genetic mutations (e.g., KCNQ1, KCNH2 but causing loss of function)
Characteristic ECG pattern with ST elevation in V1-V3
Risk of ventricular arrhythmias without short QT

redFlags: History of sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained syncope
Family history of sudden cardiac death at young age
references: Gollob MH, Redpath CJ, Roberts JD. The short QT syndrome: proposed diagnostic criteria. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2011;57(7):802-812.

Priori SG, Wilde AA, Horie M, et al. HRS/EHRA/APHRS expert consensus statement on the diagnosis and management of patients with inherited primary arrhythmia syndromes. Heart Rhythm. 2013;10(12):1932-1963.
Brugada R, Hong K, Dumaine R, et al. Sudden death associated with short-QT syndrome linked to mutations in HERG. Circulation. 2004;109(7): 830-835.
